report.summary: One action-required phantom control found: the implemented 30-minute idle-session-expiry control no longer rejects expired sessions.

findings.title: Implemented idle-session-expiry control was removed

model_excerpt.quote: Sessions idle for more than 30 minutes are rejected and the customer must sign in again, enforced on every request in internal/session/expiry.go

evidence.note: The middleware now handles an existing session only by updating its LastSeen timestamp.
Every request is forwarded to the next handler; there is no idle-time comparison, session deletion, or unauthorized response.

relevance.justification: The cited implementation is the exact file named by the implemented control, and the PR removes the behavior the control claims to enforce.

findings.agent_prompt: Update threatmodels/storefront.tm.hcl in threat "session hijacking", control "idle session expiry": the control is marked implemented = true and claims sessions idle for more than 30 minutes are rejected, but internal/session/expiry.go:11-15 now only updates LastSeen and always forwards the request. Set implemented = false, or revise the control to point to a replacement implementation that enforces the 30-minute idle timeout.
findings.suggested_fix: Set control "idle session expiry" to implemented = false, or update it to reference a restored or replacement 30-minute idle-expiry implementation.
